issue_context.title: It is no longer possible to insert a second identical unsigned attribute into a CMS/CAdES signature
issue_context.body:
Hi All,

I'm using OpenSSL 3.0.11 (previously 3.0.8).
Since this change https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/21505, it is no longer possible to insert a second identical unsigned attribute into a CMS/CAdES signature (like many archiveTimestamp attributes for example).

The problem lies in the CMS_unsigned_add1_attr_by_NID function, which relies on X509at_add1_attr_by_NID.

Thanks.
comments: **OTC: We should not revert #21505 but this needs to be investigated and possibly a different fix is needed.**

This is clearly a bug - there are multiple unsigned Attributes that can occur multiple times in a CMS signature. From RFC 5126: `The archive-time-stamp attribute is an unsigned attribute.  Several instances of this attribute may occur with an electronic signature both over time and from different TSUs.`

From RFC 5652: `The UnsignedAttributes syntax is defined as a SET OF Attributes.  The UnsignedAttributes in a signerInfo may include multiple instances of the countersignature attribute.`

review_comments: Do we care that it does this check twice?
